facts.text: Director Joseph Merhi co-founded PM Entertainment with Richard Pepin. The company name is just their surnames: Pepin-Merhi.
Before directing, Joseph Merhi owned several pizzerias around Las Vegas. He went from slinging pies to making car-crash action movies.
Continuity watch: during Jake's fight with the purse thief, all three store windows end up broken, yet the thief is thrown through one that was already smashed.
Dana Bentley (Jenny) was busy in 1990: she also turned up in Sorority House Massacre II, Bad Girls from Mars and The Invisible Maniac that same year.
Star Dan Haggerty is best known as mountain man James 'Grizzly' Adams, in a 1974 film and the NBC series The Life and Times of Grizzly Adams (1977-78).
Paul Hayes, who plays repo boss Bulldog, served in the U.S. Marine Corps artillery from 1967 to 1972, long before landing roles in Black Dynamite and Buffy.
Dan Haggerty's famous beard once caught fire in 1977 when a careless restaurant patron carried a flaming cocktail too close to him.
Before Grizzly Adams, Dan Haggerty helped build the motorcycles used in Easy Rider, and he played a non-speaking bodybuilder in Muscle Beach Party (1964).
Dan Haggerty worked as an animal trainer and stuntman, and was a Muscle Beach bodybuilder in the early 1960s, before he ever became Grizzly Adams.
The Stinker Madness podcast notes Repo Jake has a surprising amount of expensive-looking stunts for a low-budget 1990 film, and claims they were staged without permits.
Dan Haggerty is the only person to have a Hollywood Walk of Fame star removed. It was meant for actor Don Haggerty and misspelled. Dan later got a proper star near Grauman's Chinese Theatre.
Director Joseph Merhi was born in a small town in Syria and moved to Florida at 18 without speaking English. He went on to produce over 100 movies.
PM Entertainment's first film was L.A. Heat (1989) with Jim Brown. A year later came Repo Jake, one of the company's early home-video action hits.
Dan Haggerty also sold his own barbecue sauce, made from his own recipe, and in 1991 opened Haggerty's Bistro in Studio City, California.
The Slam Track scenes pay off for PM Entertainment's trademark: its films were known for car chases, gunfire and explosions over plot. Director Joseph Merhi often teamed with Richard Pepin.
Dan Haggerty was sentenced to 90 days in county jail and three years probation in 1984 for furnishing cocaine to two undercover police officers.
Repo Jake was written by Joe Hart and produced by PM Entertainment, the home-video action factory run by Joseph Merhi and Richard Pepin.
Repo Jake shows up in Ready Player One (2018), Steven Spielberg's pop-culture-packed blockbuster, according to IMDb trivia.
Reviewer Jedadiah Leland of Through the Shattered Lens wrote that Repo Jake would be unwatchable without Dan Haggerty's likability, but is still not a terrible way to spend 90 minutes.
In early 2000, Joseph Merhi and Richard Pepin sold PM Entertainment to The Harvey Entertainment Company for $6.5 million in cash plus $1.45 million in stock.
On Rotten Tomatoes, Repo Jake has no professional critic reviews at all. The audience reviews there are mostly negative, but several single out Dan Haggerty as the highlight.
PM Entertainment's library of 150-plus films, Repo Jake included, passed to Echo Bridge, then FilmRise in 2021 and then Shout! Studios.
The Stinker Madness podcast calls Repo Jake 'so bad, it's absolutely fantastic,' praising its stilted, quotable dialogue and a mix of overacting, underacting and bizarre performances.
Dan Haggerty returned as a modern Grizzly Adams in Grizzly Mountain (1997). He later appeared in Big Stan (2007) and died in January 2016, aged 73.
PM Entertainment, Repo Jake's studio, also tried kids' films such as Magic Kid and Bigfoot: The Unforgettable Encounter, with limited success compared with its action and kickboxing titles.
